mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy shift that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that triggers central bank policy support, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals broad-based demand contraction that triggers equity market flight to quality, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of RSAFS decline and HOUST decline fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During expansionary supply regimes characterized by sustained industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105.0 and rising for 3 months), corporate output expansion supports earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 105.0 and has increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) over the past month indicates strong household demand that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market deterioration that may lead to central bank rate cuts, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS decline and UNRATE increase fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may lead to aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle labor market conditions where unemployment is below 4.0% and job growth is slowing (PAYEMS growth rate < 0.5% for 3 months), the risk of overheating leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the central bank prepares to tighten.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth rate < 0.5% for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0% and PAYEMS growth rate is below 0.5% for three consecutive months.
